Abhijeet Dipke was detained at his Jhandewalan residence, while Neha Bora was picked up from Mandi House in central Delhi. The protest, called by the CJP at Central Park, was part of the party’s campaign demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Earlier in the day, Abhijeet expressed concerns over the heavy deployment of security forces to halt the Tiranga yatra. “Why are you against Tiranga,” he asked, tagging Prime Minister Narendra Modi. items.title: Chennai SIR protest: DMK MP Kanimozhi criticises SC for speaking up after damage was done
items.summary: Indirectly appearing to criticise the Supreme Court for failing to uphold the rights of crores of voters who were removed from the electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) MP Kanimozhi said on October 16 that they respond only after the “damage is done.” The MP was speaking at the protest gathering against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar held at Rajarathnam Stadium in Chennai. The protest demanded Gyanesh’s resignation and the roll back of the SIR. “Even when people expect justice, the authorities respond only after a delay. When something happens, the authorities do not speak up. Only after the damage is done do they say they did not approve it or had nothing to do with it,” Kanimozhi said referring to the Supreme Court which recently said that it did not approve the modified Form 6 declaration which necessitates the applicants to state whether they or their parents were mapped in the previous SIR. The requirement was not part of the earlier Form 6 used during SIR exercises. In the SIR taken up by the Election Commission of India (ECI), 13 crore voters have been disenfranchised, for which the opposition party including the DMK have been demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. Kanimozhi highlighted that 74 lakh people have lost their voting rights in Tamil Nadu due to the SIR. “In Kolathur, the constituency of our party leader and former Chief Minister MK Stalin, one lakh people have been removed,” the MP said, suggesting large-scale voter manipulation. The former CM lost from the constituency in the recent Assembly elections by a margin of 8,795 votes. According to the MP, only 20,000 voters were supposed to be removed from the electoral rolls in Tamil Nadu, but 74 lakh people were denied voting rights, she said. Accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the ECI of voter manipulation, the DMK leader said: “Similar actions have taken place in many parts of the country. In Maharashtra and elsewhere, names are being removed based on whether officials think people in a particular neighbourhood or household are likely to vote for the ruling party.
